route_status.proven_scope: The unchanged focused probe passes its assertions under Godot 4.7.2-stable: a post-sink tub tap starts one bounded bunny reaction; the brush is blocked during it; repeated taps and passive wait do not drain or finish the tub; the saved drained state skips the reaction; the existing tub stroke seam remains causal; and the cleanup wrapper exposes the same tap route. The receipt records exit 0, no failure lines, isolated profile, and headless scripted evidence.
route_status.gaps: The probe sets day_one_bathroom_cleanup_step = 1, directly instantiates the cleaning owner and swimmer, supplies presentation fixtures, and calls probe seams. It does not play from fresh-save bathroom entry or feed ordinary routed input through a visible room. It verifies code/state assertions, not the rendered pace or sound. No Mobile capture, physical device, child, or owner session occurred.

source_constants.value: The bunny comic reaction is 0.68 seconds; after it finishes, the drain callback waits 0.20 seconds before rebuilding the tub brush presentation.
source_constants.scope: Source-defined reaction and post-drain transition; not observed gameplay duration.

source_constants.value: The swimmer bobs at 0.72 and 1.38 radians/second with travel amplitudes supplied by its caller; its paddle oscillation uses 2.6 radians/second. Bathroom setup supplies 13 px horizontal and 3 px vertical travel.
source_constants.scope: Code motion parameters only; rendered motion and perceived pace are unreviewed.

source_constants.value: The probe waits 1.05 seconds after its repeated-tap check before asserting the drained brush stage; this is test synchronization, not a child wait-time measurement.

timing.assumptions: No child session duration is inferred. Runner wall time (16.732 seconds) is probe execution time, not gameplay timing.

tactile.target_size: The one-finger gesture surface is set to StorybookUI.CANVAS_SIZE (1280x720 base canvas); tub tap acceptance uses distance from TUB_CENTER within TUB_HALF_WIDTH + 72 px. The probe calls the tap seam at the fixed tub center, so it does not measure visible hit target size, projected phone geometry, or comfort.
tactile.press_response: A valid tub tap synchronously begins the one-shot response, hides the tap pointer/guide and parked brush, then calls the swimmer's comic animation. The probe sees state change after 0.12 seconds of test time; it does not measure rendered-frame latency or routed touch response.
tactile.drag_hold_release: After the bunny reaction and drain transition, the brush stage is enabled and back-and-forth strokes remain required; the focused probe uses scripted points and motion-time values. The bunny itself is not draggable or hold-controlled. Physical drag, hold, and release were not observed.
tactile.ownership: This probe does not establish native touch ownership for the tub tap; it calls probe_tap_tub directly. The surrounding gesture owner has single-finger behavior, but that is outside this focused proof.
tactile.cancellation: No pause/focus-loss or interruption during the bunny reaction is exercised here. The probe verifies saved drained state skips a second comic reaction on Continue.

play_appeal.hypothesis: A visibly bounded swimmer with a short comic protest can make draining feel like a response to the little character, and the subsequent brush task restores the child's agency. The very small coded bob/paddle amplitudes may read as calm pacing; only rendered phone-size review and child observation can establish whether the bunny is noticeable and the pause feels lively rather than stalled.
play_appeal.variety: The beat separates the tub tap, one comic reaction, and intentional brushing into distinct actions in code; the probe does not establish how clearly those phases read in play.
play_appeal.world_response: The swimmer reacts once and disappears during the drain reveal, according to the code path; no rendered room response was reviewed.
play_appeal.replay: Saved drained state skips the one-shot reaction and resumes with the brush stage in the probe. Child-facing re-entry and replay feel are not assessed.

observations.title: The drain beat is one bounded comic interruption, then returns control to brushing
evidence: scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:805-834 (one-shot guard, immediate prompt dismissal, and reaction start)
scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:837-855 (drain state, completion cue, 0.20-second transition, brush stage restore)
runtime/L05/attempt_1/probe.log:5-15 (one reaction, repeat/passive no-progress, bounded drain and brush enabled assertions all OK)
observations.reproduction: Run the retained L05 helper once; the receipt is PASS with zero failure lines. The probe issues one tub tap, checks the reaction, repeats the tap, waits, then checks the drained brush state.
observations.child_impact: The scripted flow gives the bunny a single reaction without awarding the tub-cleaning step; the child must still brush intentionally. Whether the 0.68-second beat is emotionally legible or feels too quick is not established by the headless run.
observations.proposed_repair: No code change is indicated by this probe. Review the exact drain-to-brush transition at normal speed on Mobile and on the target phone before tuning timing.
observations.acceptance_test: On the target phone, make the tub tap through normal input and verify the bunny's reaction is readable, finite, and followed promptly by a clear brush cue, while repeated taps cannot skip the intentional brush action.

observations.title: Swimmer motion is deliberately small and its full cutout is bounded to the water basin
evidence: scripts/games/day_one_dust_bunny_swimmer.gd:65-98 (complete visible footprint accounted for when deriving safe center bounds)
scripts/games/day_one_dust_bunny_swimmer.gd:219-232 (sinusoidal bob/paddle motion is clamped to safe center bounds)
scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd:524-536 (bathroom caller supplies 13x3 px travel and 210x100 px basin)
observations.reproduction: Inspect the bathroom caller's setup arguments and the swimmer's clamped motion. The existing probe asserts a true-2D casual swimmer state; it does not capture its movement at normal rendered speed.
observations.child_impact: Small movement may keep attention on the bathroom task and prevent the cutout from leaving the tub. It may also be hard to notice on a phone; this is a hypothesis, not a confirmed visibility defect. MA-VIS-009's pool-specific lifecycle and acceptance scope is not closed by this bathroom probe.
observations.proposed_repair: No motion change indicated. Check the existing approved art in the actual dirty-bathroom composite at phone size and normal speed; preserve the bounded motion unless visual/device evidence identifies a problem.
observations.acceptance_test: Capture the live tub scene on the supported Mobile canvas at phone aspect, inspect normal-speed bob/paddle and water contact, then verify on the target device that the swimmer is noticeable without competing with the brush cue and remains inside the tub.

observations.title: Continue preserves the drain milestone and does not replay the comic beat
evidence: scripts/probe_day_one_bathroom_bunny.gd:145-163 (serialize after drain, restore a fresh main, and assert no replay with brush cue present)
runtime/L05/attempt_1/probe.log:12 (saved drain state skips comic reaction on Continue assertion OK)
observations.reproduction: The probe serializes state after the drain has completed, restores it into a new ReefMain/cleaning owner, and asserts the reaction seam rejects another tap while the back-and-forth prompt is visible.
observations.child_impact: The tested saved milestone avoids replaying the bunny's already-seen interruption and returns to the intended next action. The test uses a saved patch rather than a full application restart or visible route.
observations.proposed_repair: No change indicated by this assertion. Keep the saved drain state idempotent and validate it through actual Continue/re-entry separately.
observations.acceptance_test: On a device, drain the tub, save/leave during the following brush stage, Continue through the visible route, and confirm the bunny reaction does not replay and the brush task remains actionable.

observations.title: Probe accepts a comic caption as evidence of the No response, not audible playback
evidence: scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:821-826 (the drain reaction calls show_msg with the text NO! and marks the voice-sent flag)
scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:998-1005 (the later drain-complete cue is routed through say_day_one_context)
scripts/probe_day_one_bathroom_bunny.gd:120-123,344-352 (probe accepts either HUD text/key or a snapshot string containing No; no playback assertion)
observations.reproduction: Inspect the No reaction call and the probe's _voice_or_caption_mentions_no helper. A passing assertion can be satisfied by a HUD caption, so it does not prove that a recording played.
observations.child_impact: A child who misses the visual may not hear the comic reaction; no absence of audio playback was demonstrated by this test, so this is an evidence gap rather than a confirmed runtime audio defect.
observations.proposed_repair: Do not alter protected voice recordings based on this result. Confirm the intended audible behavior and exact authorized cue through audio routing/device listening before reporting audio acceptance.
observations.acceptance_test: Using approved recordings and normal audio settings on the target phone, verify whether the comic No is intentionally visual-only or audible; if audible is intended, bind and listen to the exact authorized cue and ensure it is not truncated by the drain-complete instruction.

observations.title: L05 does not prove the live bathroom entry or ordinary routed tub tap
evidence: scripts/probe_day_one_bathroom_bunny.gd:42-90 (directly constructs owners and sets day_one_bathroom_cleanup_step = 1 before the focused state)
scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd:307-328 (the shared cleaning owner is mounted after supply hunt completion)
observations.reproduction: Read the probe initialization and tap calls: the test writes the post-sink state and invokes probe_tap_tub directly. It never traverses the supply hunt, visible bathroom route, or native touch path.
observations.child_impact: This run cannot establish that the child discovers the tub tap after completing the bathroom supplies, sees/hears its cue, or can progress without coaching. The open route and embodied bathroom-action findings remain outside this assertion set.
observations.proposed_repair: No gameplay defect is reproduced by this route gap alone. Perform a routed fresh-save session, and separately verify that each bathroom cleaning step shows Roshan's required local work/contact under MA-PLAY-004.
observations.acceptance_test: From fresh save on the target phone, reach the bathroom through visible gameplay, collect supplies, complete the sink, tap the tub through ordinary input, watch the bunny/drain/brush transition, then verify Roshan's local brushing action, leave/re-enter, and child comprehension without adult instruction.

strengths.strength: The focused state machine distinguishes a one-time comic drain reaction from intentional tub brushing; the retained probe passes the repeated-tap, passive-wait, and saved-drain assertions.
Bathroom swimmer setup uses true-2D art and bounds the full cutout inside the assigned basin in source.

acceptance_gaps: The PASS is limited to one exact-Godot 4.7.2 headless internal scripted probe, with direct post-sink state setup and synthetic seams; it does not establish the fresh visible route or ordinary routed input (DL-QA-02, DL-QA-03).
No displayed Mobile composition, phone-size target geometry, rendered response timing, frame pacing, or actual-device touch/audio session is present (DL-QA-03, DL-QA-04, DL-QA-07).
The probe's comic-No check accepts captions/state strings and does not establish audio playback; no child comprehension, play appeal, or owner acceptance was observed (DL-QA-05, DL-QA-06).
MA-PLAY-001 fresh-route proof and the bathroom portion of MA-PLAY-004's local Roshan travel/contact/action proof remain separate open acceptance requirements.
